title: State Department Wants Palantir’s Advice on Free Speech and “Countering Digital Surveillance”
excerpt: The State Department is asking Peter Thiel’s Palantir for advice on free speech and “countering digital surveillance.”
content_html:
The Trump administration tapped a surveillance giant with a record of attacking the press to advise the State Department on free speech.

Among the partners for the State Department’s new “Freedom Tech Excellence Program” is Palantir, the AI and data integration firm started by right-wing powerbroker Peter Thiel. Under the program, company employees will go on temporary assignments to advise the government on “digital freedom and freedom of expression,” including counter-surveillance and dealing with First Amendment issues.

“FTEP brings private sector talent to the Department for limited-term assignments to advance diplomatic efforts on key issues including online freedom of expression, privacy-enhancing technologies, countering digital surveillance, and responsible AI governance,” according to the State Department’s website.

Palantir is best known for building large-scale data analysis platforms. In addition to corporate contracts, the company’s massive government tenders include database, surveillance, and tracking tools for police and federal authorities. Among its government clients are the military, the State Department itself, and U.S. Immigrations and Customs Enforcement. Palantir and its key personnel have also been involved in multiple lawsuits against journalistic outlets.

The firm’s history has raised criticisms of its role in the new State Department initiative, especially given the Trump administration own’s dubious track record on First Amendment issues.

“To some extent, this announcement and this program sound like doublespeak,” said Carrie DeCell, a senior staff attorney at the Knight First Amendment Institute. “Certainly neither this State Department, nor the partners they have announced so far, are trustworthy leaders in what they identify as online freedom of expression or countering digital surveillance.”

The new initiative is planned to run through the beginning of 2029, according to the State Department’s press office. While participants could be placed anywhere in the agency and may require security clearances, the Freedom Tech Excellent Program “is not geared towards bolstering the Department’s internal application or operational use of AI technologies,” the department said in a statement to The Intercept.

Anduril, a military tech firm with links to Palantir and Thiel, was also listed as a partner in the State Department initiative. Anduril’s executive chair Trae Stephens is a partner at Thiel’s Founders Fund, which has invested about $2.6 billion in Anduril. Besides a mutual appreciation of “The Lord of the Rings,” Thiel shares similar politics with Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey and has backed Luckey’s new bank, Erebor.

Neither Anduril nor Palantir responded to requests for comment.

Palantir and the Feds

Palantir’s work has brought it notoriety across the globe, though at times defining what it does can be complex. It has repeatedly eschewed its label as a surveillance firm. Palantir CEO Alex Karp denied on a podcast last year that the company engages in unconstitutional surveillance work.

And, in an unsigned blog post last year, Palantir wrote, “Contrary to some media reports, we are not a surveillance company.”

Palantir, though, enabled U.S. mass surveillance by bolstering the National Security Agency’s global data collection efforts, according to documents provided to The Intercept by the whistleblower Edward Snowden. Palantir helped the NSA expand a program that became notorious for its ability to hoover up Americans’ communications along with those from abroad.

More recently, the firm has become a focal point for protests in the U.K. over its massive contract with the National Health Service and its ties to the Israeli military. Just this week, the NHS apologized after admitting it had falsely stated that Palantir did not have access to identifiable patient data.

Stateside, the company had a contract with New York City public hospitals that gave it access to patient information. The contract was allowed to expire after it came under scrutiny in an Intercept report. The Intercept also reported this year that Palantir has access to sensitive federal databases for its contract to aid in Internal Revenue Service investigations.

Palantir’s IRS work led to a letter last year from 10 members of Congress to Karp requesting information about the “mega-database” built off IRS data. In response, the firm again denied that it was engaging in widespread surveillance of Americans and that it was building any such database.

Palantir also has a 15-year relationship with ICE. The Intercept found that its contracts with the agency have aided immigration raids, including ones that led to family separations. And Palantir built bespoke software for ICE that helps track self-deportations and visa overstays.

In April, Reps. Dan Goldman and Nydia Velázquez, both Democrats from New York, sent a list of questions directed to ICE and its parent agency, the Department of Homeland Security, demanding information about how they were leveraging Palantir’s technology to create “a mass surveillance ecosystem.”

Attacks on Free Press

Along with eccentric far-right views and donations to MAGA Republicans, one of Thiel’s most well-known acts was his involvement in the lawsuit that drove the news outlet Gawker into bankruptcy.

Thiel had become upset with Gawker over the media company’s reporting about his personal life. He went on to spend $10 million secretly bankrolling lawsuits against the company, finally scoring with a major judgment in favor of the wrestler Hulk Hogan that caused Gawker to close and sell off its assets.

Journalism advocacy group Reporters Without Borders said that Thiel constituted a “serious threat” to the group’s principles of “freedom of press and independence of media,” particularly in light of the secrecy around his role in the case. His actions were, RSF said, “nothing different to governments using legal or economic leverage to shut down a media that happens to displease them.”

Palantir also recently filed a suit against Swiss online news magazine Republik for reporting on how Palantir repeatedly failed to land contracts with the Swiss government. Palantir claimed that Republik had an obligation to run a list of rebuttals from the firm.

A Swiss court, however, handed Palantir a defeat by siding with the outlet on all but one of the 23 charges and forcing Palantir to pay most of Republik’s legal fees. (In a since-deleted post on Medium responding to the Republik lawsuit, Palantir once again denied that it is a surveillance company.)

David Greene, senior counsel for anti-surveillance nonprofit Electronic Frontier Foundation, said that positioning Palantir as a bulwark for civil rights undermined the government’s own free speech initiative.

“There’s a big problem right now with the U.S. government and the people outside government who exercise power, in terms of trying to claim free speech as a value when they clearly don’t sincerely hold that value,” Greene said. “It really lowers the esteem of the U.S. in terms of having any moral authority on freedom of expression grounds.”

blocks.html_en: Along with eccentric far-right views and donations to MAGA Republicans, one of Thiel’s most well-known acts was his involvement in the lawsuit that drove the news outlet Gawker into bankruptcy.

blocks.html_en: Thiel had become upset with Gawker over the media company’s reporting about his personal life. He went on to spend $10 million secretly bankrolling lawsuits against the company, finally scoring with a major judgment in favor of the wrestler Hulk Hogan that caused Gawker to close and sell off its assets.

blocks.html_en: Journalism advocacy group Reporters Without Borders said that Thiel constituted a “serious threat” to the group’s principles of “freedom of press and independence of media,” particularly in light of the secrecy around his role in the case. His actions were, RSF said, “nothing different to governments using legal or economic leverage to shut down a media that happens to displease them.”

blocks.html_en: David Greene, senior counsel for anti-surveillance nonprofit Electronic Frontier Foundation, said that positioning Palantir as a bulwark for civil rights undermined the government’s own free speech initiative.

content_html_zh:
特朗普政府聘请了一家有攻击媒体记录的监控巨头为国务院提供有关言论自由的建议。

Palantir 是国务院新的“自由技术卓越计划”的合作伙伴之一，这是一家由右翼权力掮客 Peter Thiel 创办的人工智能和数据集成公司。 根据该计划，公司员工将执行临时任务，就“数字自由和言论自由”向政府提供建议，包括反监视和处理第一修正案问题。

美国国务院网站称，“FTEP 为国务院带来了私营部门人才，执行限期任务，以推进在网络言论自由、增强隐私技术、打击数字监控和负责任的人工智能治理等关键问题上的外交努力。”

Palantir 以构建大规模数据分析平台而闻名。 除了公司合同外，该公司的大规模政府招标还包括为警察和联邦当局提供数据库、监控和跟踪工具。 其政府客户包括军队、国务院本身以及美国移民和海关执法局。 Palantir 及其关键人员还卷入了多起针对新闻媒体的诉讼。

该公司的历史因其在国务院新举措中的作用而受到批评，特别是考虑到特朗普政府在第一修正案问题上的可疑记录。

奈特第一修正案研究所的高级专职律师卡丽·德塞尔 (Carrie DeCell) 表示：“在某种程度上，这一公告和该计划听起来像是双调。” “当然，无论是国务院还是他们迄今为止宣布的合作伙伴，在他们所认为的在线言论自由或反数字监控方面都不是值得信赖的领导者。”

据国务院新闻办公室称，这项新举措计划持续到 2029 年初。 该部门在给 The Intercept 的一份声明中表示，虽然参与者可以被安排在该机构的任何地方，并且可能需要安全许可，但 Freedom Tech Excellent 计划“并不是为了支持该部门内部应用或人工智能技术的操作使用”。

Anduril 是一家与 Palantir 和 Thiel 有联系的军事科技公司，也被列为国务院倡议的合作伙伴。 Anduril 的执行主席 Trae Stephens 是 Thiel 创始人基金的合伙人，该基金已向 Anduril 投资了约 26 亿美元。 除了对《指环王》的共同欣赏之外，蒂尔还与 Anduril 联合创始人 Palmer Luckey 有着相似的政治观点，并支持 Luckey 的新银行 Erebor。

Anduril 和 Palantir 均未回应置评请求。

Palantir 和联邦调查局

Palantir 的工作使其在全球范围内声名狼藉，尽管有时定义其功能可能很复杂。 它一再回避自己作为监控公司的标签。 Palantir 首席执行官 Alex Karp 去年在播客上否认该公司从事违宪监控工作。

Palantir 在去年一篇未署名的博客文章中写道，“与一些媒体报道相反，我们不是一家监控公司。”

不过，根据举报人爱德华·斯诺登 (Edward Snowden) 向 The Intercept 提供的文件，Palantir 通过支持国家安全局的全球数据收集工作，实现了美国的大规模监控。 Palantir 帮助美国国家安全局扩大了一项计划，该计划因能够窃取美国人与国外的通信而臭名昭著。

最近，该公司因其与英国国家医疗服务体系的巨额合同以及与以色列军方的关系而成为英国抗议活动的焦点。 就在本周，NHS 在承认错误地表示 Palantir 无法访问可识别的患者数据后道歉。

在美国境内，该公司与纽约市公立医院签订了一份合同，允许其访问患者信息。 该合同在接受 Intercept 报告的审查后被允许到期。 Intercept 今年还报道称，Palantir 可以访问敏感的联邦数据库，以获取其协助国税局调查的合同。

Palantir 的 IRS 工作导致去年 10 名国会议员致信 Karp，要求提供有关基于 IRS 数据构建的“大型数据库”的信息。 作为回应，该公司再次否认它正在对美国人进行广泛的监视，并且正在建立任何此类数据库。

Palantir 还与 ICE 有着 15 年的合作关系。 The Intercept 发现，它与该机构签订的合同协助了移民突击搜查，包括导致家庭离散的搜查行动。 Palantir 为 ICE 构建了定制软件，帮助追踪自我驱逐出境和签证逾期居留情况。

四月，众议员。 来自纽约的民主党人 Dan Goldman 和 Nydia Velázquez 向 ICE 及其上级机构国土安全部发送了一系列问题，要求提供有关他们如何利用 Palantir 技术创建“大规模监控生态系统”的信息。

对新闻自由的攻击

除了古怪的极右观点和向 MAGA 共和党人捐款之外，泰尔最著名的行为之一是他参与了导致新闻媒体 Gawker 破产的诉讼。

泰尔对 Gawker 媒体公司报道他的个人生活感到不满。 随后，他花费 1000 万美元秘密资助针对该公司的诉讼，最终做出了有利于摔跤手浩克·霍根 (Hulk Hogan) 的重大判决，导致 Gawker 关闭并出售其资产。

新闻倡导组织“记者无国界”表示，蒂尔对该组织“新闻自由和媒体独立”的原则构成了“严重威胁”，特别是考虑到他在此案中所扮演的角色保密。 无国界记者组织表示，他的行为“与政府利用法律或经济杠杆来关闭碰巧令他们不满的媒体没有什么不同。”

Palantir 最近还对瑞士在线新闻杂志 Republik 提起诉讼，因为该杂志报道了 Palantir 如何多次未能与瑞士政府签订合同。 Palantir 声称 Republik 有义务列出该公司的反驳清单。

然而，一家瑞士法院在 23 项指控中除一项之外的所有指控中都支持该媒体，并迫使 Palantir 支付 Republik 的大部分法律费用，从而判 Palantir 败诉。 （在 Medium 上回应 Republik 诉讼的帖子中，Palantir 再次否认自己是一家监控公司，该帖子现已被删除。）

反监视非营利组织电子前沿基金会的高级顾问戴维·格林 (David Greene) 表示，将 Palantir 定位为民权堡垒破坏了政府自己的言论自由倡议。

格林说：“美国政府和政府以外行使权力的人目前存在一个大问题，他们试图将言论自由视为一种价值观，而他们显然并不真诚地坚持这种价值观。” “这确实降低了美国在言论自由方面拥有道德权威的声誉。”
